recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-5192 unless PA later reopens the meaning or binding of HealthcareService.serviceProvisionCode.
issue_request: FHIR-5192 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 HealthcareService ballot comment requesting removal of misleading free-provision wording, ServiceProvisionCode naming, cardinality 0..1 to 0..*, and wording that describes conditions under which a healthcare service is available/offered.
initial_application: The historical application commit 8fb7336ca5 changed HealthcareService.freeProvisionCode to HealthcareService.serviceProvisionCode, changed the cardinality to 0..*, and replaced the old free-provision definition with the requested service-provision text. A nearby e7cc9ca414 introduction commit also mentioned FHIR-5192 but did not alter the serviceProvisionCode element.
additional_context: HealthcareService is active in source/fhir.ini. Current XML source carries the application forward as HealthcareService.serviceProvisionCode with max='*', the requested definition/comment, and a ServiceProvisionConditions binding. Current source searches found no remaining old freeProvisionCode element or old free-provision definition. Later FHIR-41782 considered but rejected using ServiceProvisionCode for referral requirements, choosing separate referralRequired/eligibility changes instead. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-5192 community conflict.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the authoritative current source already satisfies the issue's required semantic changes.

related_jiras.note: Later HealthcareService referral work considered ServiceProvisionCode as an option but chose separate referralRequired/eligibility changes, so it does not supersede FHIR-5192.
